scenes.headline: How LFM3 mixes three kinds of layer
scenes.sub: Read from its config, code and weights
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Weft! LFM3 is a small language model built from three kinds of layer. Here is what each one does, and what that does to memory.

scenes.text: Only six of its 24 layers read the whole context. The other 18 look at a few tokens or a short window, so the cache stays small.
scenes.mark: Only six of its 24 layers read the whole context.
scenes.say: Only six of the twenty four layers read the whole context. The other eighteen look at a few tokens or a short window, and that keeps the cache small.

steps.label: full attention
steps.say: A full attention layer lets each token read every earlier token. Six layers do this, and their cache grows with the text.

steps.label: window, 256 tokens
steps.say: A window layer reads only the last two hundred fifty six tokens, so its cache stops growing once the window is full.

steps.label: convolution, width 7
steps.say: A convolution layer mixes the last seven positions with one filter per channel, and keeps only six old inputs.

scenes.title: Cache at 262,144 tokens
scenes.say: At two hundred sixty two thousand tokens, twenty four full layers would need twelve thousand mebibytes of cache. This mix needs about three thousand, a quarter of that.

scenes.label: cheaper per token than 24 full layers at 128K
scenes.note: CPU microbenchmark on a loaded machine: read the shape
scenes.say: On a busy CPU, a token costs about three and a half times less than in a stack of full layers at a hundred twenty eight thousand tokens. Under four thousand, no gain.

scenes.label: benchmarks against Qwen3.5-9B
scenes.say: Liquid says the one point seven billion model can do work that needed nine billion. Its own table says fourteen wins and fifteen losses out of twenty nine.

scenes.text: A small cache is a trade: six full layers carry every long read, and the card's long-context rows show the cost.

recap: Thirteen convolution, five window, six full.
The cache is a quarter of a full stack.
Wins and losses are mixed against nine billion.
scenes.say: Thirteen convolution layers, five window, six full. The cache is a quarter of a full stack, and the wins and losses are mixed.
